heading: An honest look at what this can and can't do
intro: You deserve the real picture, not a sales pitch. Here is what people come with, and how much research genuinely stands behind each one — including the places where we simply don't know enough yet.
ctaHeading: Wondering if it could help you?
metaDescription: What this work can help with — set out honestly, alongside how much research stands behind each, including where the evidence is still thin.

conditions.name: Depression that hasn't lifted
conditions.note: This is where the evidence is strongest. For people who have tried other things without much relief, the heaviness often begins to lift within hours or days rather than weeks.

conditions.name: Depression
conditions.note: Real, meaningful relief for many people — including those who wouldn't describe their depression as severe. It tends to arrive quickly, and usually holds better with more than one visit.

conditions.name: Thoughts of ending your life
conditions.note: Among the most striking findings: these thoughts can quieten remarkably fast, sometimes within hours — often before the wider heaviness has begun to lift.

conditions.name: The low side of bipolar
conditions.note: Good evidence of real relief during the depressive stretches. Because it can occasionally tip things the other way, this is done with especially close care from your doctor.

conditions.name: The weight of past trauma
conditions.note: Encouraging results, particularly when the medicine is paired with real therapeutic support — which is exactly how it is offered here. The research is younger than it is for depression.

conditions.name: Anxiety
conditions.note: Many people find the constant background hum of worry quietens. Relief often comes quickly, though it usually takes more than one visit to settle in.

conditions.name: Obsessive thoughts and compulsions
conditions.note: Small studies have found relief from intrusive, looping thoughts in the short term. Genuinely promising, but the research is still early.

conditions.name: Drinking that has taken hold
conditions.note: Early signs suggest this work may help people drink less and return to it less often, especially alongside therapy. More research is still needed.

conditions.name: Other substance use
conditions.note: Some early, hopeful findings when paired with ongoing therapeutic support. This remains an area still being explored.

conditions.name: Eating disorders
conditions.note: A small number of studies point to possible benefit. There isn't yet enough evidence to consider this a settled path.
